title: The Frozen Throne
subtitle: Where stone dreams shatter and ice crowns the ruthless

setting.name: The Frozen Reaches
setting.description: The Frozen Reaches encompass the brutal northern coastline of Faerun where the Sea of Moving Ice grinds against the Sword Coast's northernmost settlements. This is a land defined by extremes: temperatures that plunge far below freezing for months at a time, winds that scour exposed skin raw, and a landscape of jagged ice floes, snow-buried tundra, and glacier-carved fjords that slice deep into the continental shelf. The few settlements that cling to this coast — fishing villages, whaling stations, and the occasional fortified trading post — survive through sheer stubbornness and an intimate understanding of the sea's rhythms. Now those settlements are burning. Frost giant longships, each one a hundred feet of iron-banded timber with a carved dragon prow, have been raiding the coast with unprecedented frequency and savagery. Entire villages have been carried off — not just their wealth, but their people, dragged aboard longships in chains and hauled north into the grinding ice. Inland, the situation is stranger still. The stone giant caverns of Deadstone Cleft, normally sealed to outsiders, have gone silent. The rhythmic hammering that once echoed from the deep places has stopped, replaced by an unnatural quiet that the local dwarves find deeply unsettling. Two giant crises converge here: the frost giants' aggressive campaign to find the legendary Ring of Winter, and the stone giants' spiritual collapse as their millennia-old communion with the earth was shattered along with the Ordning.
setting.atmosphere: The dominant sound is wind — a ceaseless, keening howl that strips warmth from flesh and carries the salt-spray of the sea hundreds of yards inland. The northern lights ripple across the sky in curtains of green and violet, casting an otherworldly glow over the snow-fields that makes the landscape look like another plane entirely. During the brief hours of winter daylight, the sun hangs low and orange on the horizon, painting the ice in shades of amber and blood. At night, the stars are viciously bright in the clear arctic air, and the aurora provides enough light to navigate by — which is fortunate, because torches and lanterns attract frost giant scouts the way campfires attract moths. The cold is a constant, physical presence that must be actively resisted. Breath freezes in the air. Metal sticks to exposed skin. Water left uncovered becomes ice within minutes. And beneath it all, beneath the wind and the cold and the grinding of ice floes, there is a deeper sound: a subsonic vibration that makes teeth ache and bones hum, as if the earth itself is in pain.

keyLocations.name: The Icebound Coast
keyLocations.description: The Icebound Coast stretches for two hundred miles along Faerun's northwestern shore, a jagged line of frozen cliffs, ice-choked harbors, and wind-scoured beaches. Before the frost giant raids, a chain of small but prosperous fishing villages dotted the coastline, connected by a narrow track called the Shore Road that wound between the cliffs and the sea. Now the Shore Road is a gallery of destruction. Villages that stood for generations have been reduced to charred timbers and frozen blood. Longship keels have gouged furrows in the harbor beaches like the claw marks of enormous beasts. The surviving settlements have pulled back from the coast, fortifying hilltop positions and posting constant watch for the telltale sight of dragon-prowed longships emerging from the sea fog. The cold here is relentless and dangerous: characters without cold weather gear or magical protection must contend with exposure, and the terrain itself — ice-slick rocks, snowdrifts that conceal crevasses, and frozen streams that can crack under weight — poses constant environmental hazards. The coast also holds beauty, though: the northern lights reflecting off the ice create displays of heartbreaking splendor, and the silence between storms has a purity that borders on the sacred.
features: Frozen Cliffs (60-100 ft high) — DC 16 Athletics to climb with proper gear, DC 20 without; falling into the sea below deals 3d6 bludgeoning + 2d6 cold damage; DC 14 Perception to spot handholds that reduce the climb to DC 12

Ice-Choked Harbors — the sea ice extends 100+ ft from shore; DC 14 Acrobatics to move across at full speed, DC 10 at half speed; ice can crack under more than 500 lbs (DC 15 Dexterity save or fall into frigid water: 4d6 cold damage, DC 13 Constitution save each round or gain 1 level of exhaustion)

Shore Road (narrow coastal track) — passable but treacherous in winter; DC 12 Survival to navigate without losing time, DC 10 with a local guide; ambush points every half mile where the road passes between cliff faces

Northern Lights — the aurora provides dim light across the entire region at night; DC 16 Arcana check reveals the aurora is unnaturally intense, amplified by the breaking of the Ordning; spellcasters who meditate under the aurora for 1 hour gain advantage on one Arcana check within the next 24 hours

Extreme Cold — characters without cold weather clothing or equivalent magical protection must make DC 10 Constitution saves every hour or gain 1 level of exhaustion; this DC increases to 13 during blizzards and 15 during supernatural cold events
encounters: A frost giant longship (1 frost giant captain, 2 frost giant warriors, 8 winter wolves) raiding a coastal village — the party can intervene from shore, attempt to board the longship, or organize the villagers' defense

A pack of 6 winter wolves hunting along the Shore Road, driven south by the frost giants' expansion — they are unusually aggressive and fight to the death rather than flee, suggesting supernatural influence

A pair of ice mephit scouts (2 ice mephits) spying on a surviving settlement on behalf of the frost giants — they can be captured and interrogated (they speak Aquan and Auran) for intelligence about Svardborg's defenses
secrets: One of the raided villages, Skaldheim, was not destroyed randomly — the frost giants were specifically searching for a local legend about the Ring of Winter being hidden 'where the ice meets the stone,' which the villagers interpreted as their coastal caves; the caves are empty, but the search pattern reveals how desperately Jarl Storvald wants the Ring

A surviving fisherman named Old Bjarni witnessed a frost giant longship returning to Svardborg and can describe the iceberg-fortress's harbor entrance and the massive ice-gate that seals it — his information is accurate but three weeks old, and defenses may have changed

Beneath the frozen harbor of the destroyed village of Frostholm, a merfolk trading post survives intact — the merfolk have been observing the frost giant longships and can provide precise patrol routes and schedules in exchange for help recovering stolen merfolk artifacts from Svardborg

keyLocations.name: Deadstone Cleft
keyLocations.description: Deadstone Cleft is a vast system of natural caverns in the Graypeak Mountains, expanded and sculpted over millennia by stone giant artisans into a living gallery of their race's history and spiritual practice. The entrance is a vertical fissure in a granite cliff face, three hundred feet tall and barely twenty feet wide at the base, opening into a descending passage of smooth stone that bears the marks of countless giant hands. Before the Ordning shattered, Deadstone Cleft was a place of profound contemplation — stone giants would spend decades here, communing with the living rock through meditation and artistic expression, carving enormous bas-reliefs that told the story of giantkind from the dawn of the world. The rhythmic sound of chisel on stone echoed from the depths at all hours, a heartbeat of creativity that nearby dwarven settlements could feel through the mountain itself. Now the heartbeat has stopped. The silence from Deadstone Cleft is absolute and unnatural. The stone giants within have been thrown into spiritual crisis by the Ordning's collapse. Their connection to the earth — the fundamental aspect of their identity — has been disrupted. Some have retreated into catatonic meditation, sitting motionless for weeks. Others have gone mad, attacking their own artwork in frenzies of destruction, shattering centuries of masterwork carvings. The cleft has become a place of grief and madness, and the few stone giants who retain their sanity are desperately trying to hold their community together.
features: Entrance Fissure (300 ft tall, 20 ft wide at base) — the narrow entrance provides natural defense; DC 14 Stealth to enter unobserved during daylight, DC 10 at night; the acoustic properties of the fissure amplify sound, meaning combat or loud activity within 100 ft of the entrance echoes for miles

Meditation Chambers (various sizes, 30-100 ft ceilings) — the stone here has been worked so smooth it reflects light like dark glass; DC 16 Arcana to detect residual earth magic in the walls; a character who meditates here for 1 hour with a successful DC 14 Wisdom check gains temporary proficiency in mason's tools or stonecunning until the next long rest

Bas-Relief Galleries (walls covered in carved scenes) — DC 13 History to read and interpret the stone giant historical carvings; DC 17 to discern the prophetic carvings that depict possible futures, including one showing the Ordning restored

Crystal Veins (natural crystal formations in deeper chambers) — provide dim light throughout the cleft in shifting colors; DC 15 Nature to identify the crystals as earth-attuned resonance stones that amplify the stone giants' communion with the mountain; the crystals hum at a frequency felt in the bones rather than heard

Collapsed Sections (where maddened giants have destroyed walls) — DC 14 Acrobatics to navigate rubble fields, DC 12 Athletics to clear blocked passages; some collapses have exposed previously sealed chambers containing even older carvings
encounters: A maddened stone giant (1 stone giant, CR 7, HP 126) attacking a centuries-old bas-relief depicting the founding of Ostoria — the giant is in a dissociative state, oblivious to anything except the carving it is destroying; can be subdued with a DC 18 Persuasion check using knowledge of stone giant culture, or fought

A pair of galeb duhr (2 galeb duhr, CR 6, HP 85 each) that were awakened by the stone giants' distress and now guard a meditation chamber containing catatonic giants — they attack anything that approaches, viewing all non-stone creatures as threats to their vulnerable charges

A stone giant oracle named Thane Kayalithica and her two attendants (3 stone giants total) performing a ritual to stabilize the cavern system — they initially perceive the party as hallucinations from the dream-world and react with detached curiosity rather than hostility
secrets: The deepest meditation chamber contains a Resonance Crystal — a massive formation of earth-attuned crystal that served as the focal point for the stone giants' communion with the mountain; it has cracked since the Ordning shattered, and repairing it (DC 18 Arcana check while channeling earth-based magic, or using Mending at 5th level or higher) would restore sanity to the maddened giants and earn Kayalithica's eternal gratitude

One of the prophetic carvings, hidden behind a collapsed wall (DC 16 Investigation to discover), depicts a scene of all six giant races standing in council before a storm giant king — this is a prophecy of the Ordning's restoration and provides a crucial clue for the larger campaign

A secret passage behind the oldest carvings (DC 18 Investigation or automatically discovered by a character with stonecunning) leads to a natural underground river that flows north toward Svardborg — the stone giants used this route for trade with the frost giants in ages past, and it provides a hidden approach to the iceberg-fortress

keyLocations.name: The Dream Galleries
keyLocations.description: The Dream Galleries are the deepest and most sacred chambers of Deadstone Cleft, accessible only through a narrow passage that descends for nearly a mile beneath the mountain. These are the chambers where the most skilled stone giant artisans created their masterworks — enormous bas-reliefs that do not merely depict history but seem to LIVE. The carvings here are so detailed, so imbued with earth magic, that they shift and move in the peripheral vision, replaying ancient events in slow, grinding stone motion. The galleries chronicle the entire history of giantkind: the creation of Ostoria, the war with the dragons, the establishment of the Ordning by Annam All-Father, the rise and fall of giant civilizations, and — on the deepest walls — prophetic visions of possible futures. The air here is thick with residual magic, and the walls pulse with a slow, deep rhythm that syncs with the heartbeat of anyone who stands still long enough. For stone giants, these galleries are a place of profound spiritual significance — entering them is akin to entering a cathedral. For other creatures, the experience is disorienting and dreamlike. The boundary between past, present, and future blurs. Characters may experience brief visions or hear whispered fragments of ancient Giant speech. The galleries are both a puzzle area (reading the carvings provides crucial information) and a potential combat zone (maddened giants have followed the magic here, and the prophetic carvings can manifest dangerous illusions).
features: Living Bas-Reliefs (walls that move) — the carvings shift in peripheral vision, replaying historical events; DC 14 Perception to focus on a specific carving and watch its 'scene' play out; DC 16 History to correctly interpret what is being shown; DC 18 Arcana to interact with a carving and ask it a question (functions as Legend Lore once per carving)

Resonance Crystal Chamber (deepest point) — the central crystal formation fills a 30-ft diameter chamber; it is cracked but still functional; a DC 18 Arcana check reveals it can be repaired with concentrated earth magic; the crystal provides truesight to anyone touching it while meditating (requires DC 15 Wisdom check and 10 minutes of meditation)

Prophetic Wall (sealed behind collapse) — DC 16 Investigation to discover; the carvings here depict possible futures and provide crucial clues about the Ordning's restoration; reading them requires DC 14 History and the ability to read Giant

Dream Fog (magical atmosphere) — characters in the galleries must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom save upon entry or become charmed by the visions for 1 hour, wandering among the carvings in a trance; charmed characters are not hostile but are unresponsive and vulnerable; the effect ends if the character takes damage

Acoustic Resonance — the galleries amplify certain frequencies; thunder damage deals an extra 1d6 in this space; the Shatter spell is particularly devastating here, dealing maximum damage and potentially destroying irreplaceable carvings
encounters: 2 maddened stone giants (CR 7, HP 126 each) who have descended into the galleries and are destroying prophetic carvings in a frenzy — they can be calmed if the Resonance Crystal is repaired, or fought; fighting risks destroying priceless carvings (each missed attack that hits a wall destroys one carving permanently)

The Dream Guardian — a galeb duhr elder (use galeb duhr stats with HP 120, AC 18, and the ability to cast Stone Shape 3/day and Wall of Stone 1/day) that protects the Resonance Crystal; it allows passage to anyone who demonstrates reverence for stone (DC 14 Religion check with knowledge of stone giant customs, or DC 16 Persuasion explaining peaceful intent)

Phantom visions — the prophetic carvings manifest illusions of ancient battles when disturbed; these function as a Phantasmal Force effect (DC 15 Intelligence save or perceive the illusions as real for 1 minute, taking 1d6 psychic damage per round from phantom weapons)
secrets: The Resonance Crystal, once repaired, reveals a vision to whoever touches it: the image of Jarl Storvald torturing a cloud giant prisoner in Svardborg, demanding to know the location of the Ring of Winter; this vision provides both motivation and tactical intelligence for Act 3

One of the prophetic carvings depicts a scene that has not yet happened: the party standing before a storm giant king in an undersea court, presenting artifacts gathered from multiple giant strongholds; this is a preview of the campaign's climax and should be described to the players in evocative but vague terms

Hidden behind the Resonance Crystal is a small niche containing a Dream Crystal — a palm-sized fragment of the main crystal that grants one use of Contact Other Plane without risk of madness; this is the stone giants' greatest gift and is only given to those who repair the Resonance Crystal

keyLocations.name: Svardborg
keyLocations.description: Svardborg is not merely a fortress but an iceberg — a massive, naturally-formed berg that Jarl Storvald has claimed, hollowed out, and transformed into the greatest frost giant stronghold on the Sea of Moving Ice. From the surface, it appears as an enormous slab of blue-white ice rising eighty feet above the waterline, roughly a quarter mile across, with crude towers and platforms of ice and timber built on the flat upper surface. But the true fortress lies beneath: the iceberg extends three hundred feet below the waterline, and the frost giants have carved an entire complex of chambers, halls, and passages into its frozen heart. The centerpiece is the Great Hall of Storvald, a cathedral-sized cavern of ice with pillars carved in the likeness of frost giant heroes and a throne of solid ice upon which Jarl Storvald holds court. A frozen harbor on the iceberg's leeward side shelters six frost giant longships, sealed behind a massive gate of reinforced ice that can be raised and lowered by chains. The fortress is defended by frost giant warriors, winter wolves, and the sheer lethality of the arctic environment — the surrounding water is cold enough to kill an unprotected swimmer in minutes, and the iceberg's surface is an exposed killing field with no cover. Svardborg is a military installation, austere and functional, with none of the crude whimsy of the hill giant steading. Everything here serves a purpose, and that purpose is war.
features: Ice Gate Harbor — a frozen harbor sheltering 6 longships, sealed by a 40-ft ice gate (AC 18, HP 200) raised by iron chains; DC 20 Thieves' Tools to sabotage the chain mechanism, DC 18 Athletics to climb the gate from outside; the harbor water is frigid (4d6 cold damage per round, DC 15 Con save or paralyzed by cold)

Surface Platforms — timber-and-ice structures on the iceberg's top surface; exposed to wind (ranged attacks suffer disadvantage at ranges over 60 ft due to gale); frost giant sentries have advantage on Perception checks from the elevated platforms; DC 16 Stealth to cross the surface undetected

Ice Tunnels (interior passages) — carved from solid ice, 15-20 ft wide, 12 ft tall; the walls reflect light unpredictably, granting disadvantage on Perception checks based on sight; the ice floor is slippery (DC 12 Acrobatics to maintain footing during combat, failure = fall prone); secret passages are nearly invisible (DC 18 Investigation to detect, as they appear identical to solid ice walls)

Great Hall of Storvald (central chamber) — 100 ft long, 60 ft wide, 40 ft ceiling; ice pillars carved as frost giant heroes provide half cover; the ice throne at the far end radiates cold (creatures within 10 ft take 1d6 cold damage at the start of their turn unless resistant); acoustic properties carry whispers from one end to the other

Prison Cells (below the Great Hall) — iron-barred cells carved into the ice; Countess Mirran, a captured cloud giant, is held here; the cells are warded against teleportation (Dimensional Anchor effect); DC 16 Thieves' Tools to pick the locks, or DC 22 Strength to bend the bars
encounters: Surface patrol: 2 frost giants (CR 8, HP 138 each) and 4 winter wolves (CR 3, HP 75 each) patrolling the iceberg surface — they have advantage on Perception from elevation and the wolves' keen hearing; the patrol follows a predictable pattern (DC 14 Perception from a distance to time it, creating a 5-minute window for crossing)
Harbor ambush: if the party approaches by sea, 1 frost giant + 2 winter wolves on each side of the harbor entrance, with the ice gate ready to drop and trap intruders inside

Great Hall feast: Jarl Storvald hosts a feast for his warriors (4 frost giants, 6 winter wolves, 12 ice mephit servants) — the feast provides both a distraction opportunity and a chance to challenge the Jarl to a contest of strength according to frost giant tradition
secrets: Countess Mirran, the imprisoned cloud giant, knows the location of the second Conch of Teleportation — Storvald keeps it in a locked chest in his personal quarters behind the Great Hall; she will share this information if freed and will serve as a powerful ally in combat (use cloud giant stats: CR 9, HP 200, AC 14)

The iceberg's structural integrity depends on a natural cold-water spring in its deepest level; if the spring is contaminated or heated (e.g., by a Fireball or similar effect), the entire iceberg begins to crack — this takes 1 hour, but the threat alone may be sufficient leverage in negotiations with Storvald

Jarl Storvald's obsession with the Ring of Winter has made him paranoid and erratic; his own warriors are beginning to question his leadership; a DC 16 Insight check during any interaction with frost giant warriors reveals their unease, and a DC 18 Persuasion check can turn individual warriors neutral during the final confrontation

A hidden passage in the ice tunnels (DC 18 Investigation) leads to Storvald's private shrine to Thrym, god of frost giants — the shrine contains a Frost Brand longsword offered as tribute but never claimed, along with Storvald's personal journal written in Giant, which details his search for the Ring of Winter and provides intelligence about other frost giant operations

keyLocations.name: Storvald's War Room
keyLocations.description: Behind the Great Hall, accessible through a guarded ice corridor, lies Jarl Storvald's personal war room and living quarters. This is the nerve center of the frost giant raiding operation — a chamber thirty feet across with walls of carved ice depicting frost giant victories, a massive table of polished whalebone displaying a crude but accurate map of the Sword Coast marked with raiding targets, and a locked iron chest containing the Conch of Teleportation. Unlike the communal austerity of the rest of Svardborg, this chamber shows signs of obsessive personality: the walls are covered in scratched notes and diagrams related to the Ring of Winter, written in a frantic hand that suggests deteriorating mental state. Scrolls and books — clearly stolen from scholars and wizards during raids — are piled on every surface, opened to pages about ancient artifacts, ice magic, and the Arcane Brotherhood. A sleeping platform of piled furs occupies one corner, but it appears unused; the half-melted candles and scattered pages suggest Storvald has not slept in days. The war room reveals the Jarl not as a mighty conqueror but as a desperate, obsessed leader driving his people toward ruin in pursuit of an artifact that may not even exist in the form he imagines.
features: Whalebone War Table — the map shows all coastal settlements with symbols indicating which have been raided (crossed out), which are next (circled), and which are suspected to hold Ring of Winter clues (starred); DC 12 Investigation to read the symbols, providing complete intelligence about frost giant strategic plans

Locked Iron Chest (contains the Conch) — DC 18 Thieves' Tools to pick, DC 22 Strength to force open; trapped with a Glyph of Warding (DC 15 Investigation to detect, DC 14 Dexterity save or 5d8 cold damage); Storvald carries the key on his person

Research Documents — scattered across every surface; DC 14 Investigation to find useful information about the Ring of Winter (it is real, it grants control over ice and cold, and it was last seen in Chult centuries ago — not on the Sword Coast); DC 16 to find a letter from the Arcane Brotherhood offering to help Storvald find the Ring in exchange for an alliance

Shrine to Thrym (hidden alcove) — DC 16 Investigation or DC 14 Religion to locate; contains the Frost Brand longsword, a block of never-melting ice worth 500 gp to the right buyer, and Storvald's personal journal
encounters: 2 frost giant guards (CR 8, HP 138 each) stationed at the corridor entrance — they fight to the death to protect the Jarl's quarters; they can be lured away by a distraction in the Great Hall (DC 15 Deception to create a convincing ruse)

If the party reaches the war room while Storvald is alive and aware of intruders, he makes his final stand here with 1 frost giant champion (use frost giant stats with HP 160 and +10 to hit) — the confined space limits movement but also prevents the giants from using their full mobility
secrets: Storvald's journal reveals that he captured Countess Mirran because cloud giants are known to possess ancient maps showing the locations of powerful artifacts; he has been torturing her for weeks, but she genuinely does not know where the Ring of Winter is — she was captured because of a misunderstanding based on an old legend

The letter from the Arcane Brotherhood is signed by a wizard named Zellix, who offers Storvald magical resources in exchange for frost giant muscle — this is a plot thread that connects to other campaign scenarios involving the Brotherhood's machinations

Hidden beneath the sleeping furs (DC 14 Investigation) is a Cloak of the Manta Ray that Storvald stole from a sea elf ambassador he killed — the cloak is in perfect condition and is one of the scenario's major treasure items

synopsis: The Frozen Throne weaves together two distinct giant crises into a single epic narrative arc. The frost giants of the Sea of Moving Ice, led by the obsessive Jarl Storvald, have launched an unprecedented campaign of coastal raiding in search of the legendary Ring of Winter — an artifact of terrible power that Storvald believes will allow him to plunge the world into an eternal ice age and establish frost giant supremacy over the new Ordning. His raids have devastated coastal communities and drawn the party north into some of the most hostile terrain in Faerun. But the frost giant threat is complicated by a parallel crisis among the stone giants. In the caverns of Deadstone Cleft, the contemplative stone giants have been thrown into spiritual collapse by the Ordning's shattering. Their millennia-old communion with the living rock has been disrupted, driving some into catatonia and others into destructive madness. The stone giant oracle Thane Kayalithica represents the last hope for her people's sanity, and she offers the party both crucial context about the larger giant crisis and a hidden passage to Svardborg in exchange for help restoring her people's spiritual focus. The scenario takes the party from the devastated Icebound Coast through the haunted wonder of the stone giant meditation caverns and into the frozen heart of Svardborg itself, where they must navigate frost giant politics, free a captured cloud giant countess, and confront Jarl Storvald in his own stronghold. The discovery of a second Conch of Teleportation continues the thread toward Maelstrom and the campaign's ultimate resolution. The scenario is darker and more complex than The Hill Giant Gluttony, with moral ambiguity in the stone giant sections and genuine danger in the frost giant fortress.
hook: The party arrives at the coastal settlement of Bryn Shander — or what remains of it. The trading post, normally bustling with fishermen and fur traders, is a ghost town. Half the buildings are empty, their owners fled south. The harbor is frozen solid, and not by natural winter ice: the surface is too smooth, too uniform, with a faint blue luminescence that speaks of magical cold. The remaining residents huddle in the fortified trading hall, and their eyes carry the hollow look of people who have seen their world end in slow motion. The trading post's factor, a weathered half-elf woman named Dashara Erold, meets the party at the gate with a crossbow in one hand and a bottle of cheap whiskey in the other. 'You're either very brave or very lost,' she says. 'Three longships hit Skaldheim last week. Took everyone. Every man, woman, and child — just loaded them onto the ships and sailed north into the ice. Before that it was Frostholm. Before that, Iron Inlet. They are working their way south, and we are next.' She takes a long pull from the bottle and stares at the frozen harbor. 'But that is not even the strangest part. Two days ago, a stone giant walked out of the mountains. Sixteen feet tall, covered in dust, with eyes like a sleepwalker. She walked straight through the market square, looked at the sky, said one word — shattered — and walked into the sea. She did not come back up.' Dashara looks at the party. 'Something is very, very wrong with the giants. All of them. And if someone does not figure out what, there will not be a coast left to save.'

acts.title: Act 1: The Icebound Coast
acts.description: The first act establishes the dual threat facing the party: the immediate, visceral danger of frost giant raids on the coast and the deeper, stranger crisis among the stone giants. The party arrives at the devastated coast, witnesses or intervenes in a frost giant attack, and makes contact with Thane Kayalithica, the stone giant oracle who can explain what is happening to her people and, crucially, why the frost giants are so aggressive. Kayalithica reveals that Jarl Storvald seeks the Ring of Winter, an artifact powerful enough to trigger an eternal ice age. She offers passage through the stone giant caverns and a hidden route to Svardborg in exchange for help restoring her people's shattered spiritual communion. The act balances combat (coastal raids), exploration (finding the stone giant entrance), and deep roleplay (the encounter with Kayalithica, who initially treats the party as hallucinations from the dream-world).
objectives: Investigate the frost giant raids along the Icebound Coast
Defend or evacuate a coastal settlement under frost giant attack
Make contact with Thane Kayalithica at Deadstone Cleft's entrance
Learn about the Ordning's shattering and the Ring of Winter threat
Agree to help the stone giants in exchange for passage through the caverns and intelligence about Svardborg

scenes.name: The Raid on Iron Inlet
scenes.description: The party witnesses a frost giant longship attacking a small fishing village. This is their first encounter with frost giants — creatures far more dangerous and organized than the hill giants of the previous scenario. The frost giants fight with military discipline, coordinated tactics, and a chilling efficiency that makes the hill giant raids look like tantrums by comparison. The scene is designed to establish the frost giant threat as qualitatively different: these are not dimwitted brutes but cunning, ruthless warriors who fight in formation and cover each other. The village is small enough that the party can make a meaningful difference, but the frost giants are powerful enough that a straight fight is extremely dangerous.
scenes.readAloud: "You hear the screaming before you see the village. It carries across the frozen tundra with terrible clarity — the shrill, desperate sound of people who know they cannot escape. Iron Inlet appears around a headland: a cluster of twenty buildings huddled around a natural harbor, protected from the sea wind by a curving cliff. Or it was protected. A frost giant longship sits in the harbor mouth like a wolf in a sheepfold, its dragon prow carved from a single massive tree trunk and painted in whorls of blue and white. The ship is enormous — a hundred feet of iron-banded timber with a single mast bearing a sail of bleached white hide. And the giants are already ashore. You count three of them, each standing twenty-one feet tall, their blue-white skin stark against the grey stone buildings. They move with a practiced efficiency that chills you more than the arctic wind. One guards the longship, a greataxe resting on its shoulder, its gaze sweeping the harbor approaches with professional alertness. The other two are working through the village systematically — kicking in doors, dragging out screaming inhabitants, and herding them toward the longship with casual backhand swings of their weapons that send villagers tumbling across the ice. This is not a raid. It is a harvest. Winter wolves — enormous, frost-rimed beasts with ice-blue eyes and intelligence that borders on sapient — lope between the buildings, cutting off escape routes and driving stragglers back toward the giants with snapping jaws. A child breaks free from the group being herded to the ship and sprints toward the cliff path. A winter wolf cuts her off, snarling, its breath crystallizing in the air. The child screams. The wolf does not lunge — it simply blocks the path and waits, patient as a glacier, for the giant to collect its property."

skillChecks.success: The character spots a pattern in the frost giants' operation: the longship guard rotates position every few minutes to watch different approaches, creating brief windows of vulnerability on the harbor side. Timing an attack to coincide with the rotation grants surprise on the harbor guard.
skillChecks.failure: The operation appears seamlessly coordinated. No vulnerabilities are apparent.

skillChecks.success: The party approaches the village through a sea cave that opens into the harbor, bypassing the wolves' perimeter. They emerge within 30 ft of the longship and can choose their first target.
skillChecks.failure: A winter wolf catches the party's scent and howls an alert. The frost giants are aware of the party's presence and prepare to fight — no surprise round.

skillChecks.success: The character identifies the winter wolves' coordination as pack behavior directed by the frost giants — killing or incapacitating the nearest frost giant will cause the wolves in its squad to act independently (losing their coordinated tactics) for 1d4 rounds.
skillChecks.failure: The wolves appear to be independent predators. No tactical insight gained.

skillChecks.success: The character climbs the longship's hull and reaches the deck, gaining access to the ship's rigging and mast. From the mast, they have a commanding view of the battle and can make ranged attacks with advantage against all ground-level targets.
skillChecks.failure: The ice-slicked hull defeats the climber. They fall into the harbor water — 2d6 cold damage, DC 13 Constitution save or paralyzed for 1 round.

enemies: 3 Frost Giants (CR 8, HP 138 each, AC 15 — patchwork armor and thick hide)
4 Winter Wolves (CR 3, HP 75 each, AC 13 — Cold Breath recharge 5-6, 4d8 cold damage in 15-ft cone, DC 12 Dex save for half)
combatEncounters.tactics: The frost giants fight in coordinated pairs while the third guards the longship and the captives. The paired giants use a shield-wall tactic: one engages in melee while the other throws rocks from 30 ft behind, switching when the melee giant takes significant damage. The winter wolves operate as flankers, using their Cold Breath on grouped enemies and then engaging in melee to prevent retreat. If the longship guard is engaged, it blows a horn that calls the wolves to its position within 1 round. If two frost giants fall, the third retreats to the longship and attempts to flee with whatever captives are already aboard — the party has 2 rounds to prevent this. The frost giants do NOT fight to the death; they value their own survival and will retreat to the longship if the battle turns decisively against them. This is important: they are soldiers, not berserkers.
combatEncounters.terrain: Iron Inlet is a cramped harbor village. Buildings provide full cover but have AC 12, HP 20 and can be smashed through by giants in one action. The harbor is frozen solid (slippery: DC 12 Acrobatics to move at full speed in combat, failure = fall prone). The longship is moored 20 ft from shore, accessible via a gangplank (5 ft wide, no railing) or by crossing the ice. The cliff path on the north side of the village provides elevation (30 ft above the harbor) and half cover from the cliff face. The sea cave entrance on the south side opens into the harbor behind the longship. Village streets are narrow (10 ft wide) and provide limited sight lines — frost giants must duck to see down them.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This scene should be terrifying. Frost giants are CR 8 — significantly more dangerous than the hill giants from the previous scenario. The party should feel the power differential immediately. These are professional warriors, not gluttonous raiders. They fight smart, cover each other, and retreat when outmatched. The winter wolves add tactical complexity: they are intelligent enough to coordinate with the giants and dangerous enough to threaten any party member caught alone. The captive villagers add moral urgency: the party cannot simply flee or wait for a better opportunity. If the party drives off the raiders, the surviving villagers are grateful but broken. They provide information about the pattern of raids (working south along the coast) and rumors about a 'great ice castle' to the north. If any frost giants escape, they report back to Svardborg, potentially increasing defenses in Act 3. If the party captures a frost giant (DC 20 grapple to restrain, or reduce to 0 HP and stabilize), they can learn about Jarl Storvald's obsession with the Ring of Winter through DC 15 Intimidation.
loot: Frost giant equipment: 3 greataxes (giant-sized, worth 30 gp each as scrap metal), 3 chain shirts (giant-sized, worth 50 gp as raw chain links), 6 rocks (giant-sized throwing rocks, each weighing 60 lbs)

From the longship cargo hold: 80 gp in stolen trade goods, 3 barrels of preserved fish, 2 casks of mead, a bundle of fine white fox furs worth 200 gp, and a locked strongbox (DC 14 Thieves' Tools) containing 120 gp and a navigational chart showing Svardborg's location relative to known landmarks
Winter wolf pelts: 4 pelts worth 25 gp each if properly harvested (DC 14 Survival); the pelts provide cold resistance when worn as a cloak (DM discretion on duration)
Villagers' gratitude: free lodging, supplies, and a local guide who knows the mountain passes leading to Deadstone Cleft

scenes.name: The Stone Giant's Dream
scenes.description: Following information from the coastal settlements and guided by local knowledge, the party travels inland to the Graypeak Mountains and the entrance to Deadstone Cleft. Here they encounter Thane Kayalithica, the stone giant oracle, and her attendants. The encounter is unlike anything in the scenario so far: the stone giants do not attack, do not flee, and do not immediately acknowledge the party's existence. Kayalithica is deep in meditation at the entrance to the cleft, trying to re-establish her connection with the earth, and she perceives the party as dream-figures — hallucinations drifting through the meditation-space between the real world and the stone. This scene requires patience and creativity from the players, as brute force is counterproductive and the key to gaining the stone giants' aid is understanding and empathy.
scenes.readAloud: "The entrance to Deadstone Cleft is a wound in the mountain — a vertical fissure three hundred feet tall and barely twenty feet wide, as if some god drove an axe into the granite and left it there. The stone on either side is unnervingly smooth, polished by millennia of stone giant hands to a mirror finish that reflects the grey sky in dark, distorted images. And at the base of this fissure, sitting cross-legged on a shelf of living rock with her eyes closed and her palms pressed flat against the mountain face, is the largest stone giant you have ever seen. She is eighteen feet tall even sitting down, her skin the grey of weathered granite, her hair a cascade of crystalline threads that catch the light like quartz veins in a cliff face. She wears a robe of woven stone fiber — impossibly delicate, like chainmail made of pebbles — and her face, even in meditation, carries an expression of profound grief. The air around her vibrates with a subsonic hum that you feel in your teeth and bones. Two other stone giants stand flanking the entrance, but their posture is wrong — they are not guarding it, they are holding onto the cliff face for support, their eyes unfocused, their mouths moving silently as if reciting something they can barely remember. The ground beneath your feet trembles slightly with each of the oracle's breaths. And then, without opening her eyes, she speaks. Her voice is like gravel shifting in a riverbed — deep, slow, and carrying the weight of centuries. 'More dreamwalkers,' she says, her Giant words rumbling through the stone. 'Small ones. Warm-blooded. They come and go in the dream like sparks. Are you sparks? Or are you real?' Her brow furrows. 'I have forgotten how to tell the difference. The Ordning... the great pattern... is broken. Everything is broken. The stone weeps. Can you hear it weeping?' She opens one eye — an eye like a geode, all crystalline facets and shifting mineral colors — and regards you with the detached curiosity of someone examining an interesting insect. 'You are very small,' she observes. 'But you are here. In my dream. Or in the world. Perhaps there is no difference anymore.'"

skillChecks.success: The character's words anchor Kayalithica in reality. She blinks, truly seeing the party for the first time, and realizes they are real. 'Forgive me,' she says, her voice gaining focus. 'The world has become... uncertain. You are flesh-walkers. Small ones. Why have you come to the place of dreaming?'
skillChecks.failure: Kayalithica remains convinced the party is part of her meditation. She speaks to them as dream-figures, offering cryptic but unhelpful observations. Another approach is needed.

skillChecks.success: The character recognizes the signs of a disrupted spiritual communion and knows that stone giants ground themselves through physical contact with worked stone. Offering to touch the cliff face alongside Kayalithica — or presenting a worked stone object — helps anchor her in reality (grants advantage on subsequent Persuasion).
skillChecks.failure: The character knows stone giants are spiritual but cannot determine how to help with this specific crisis.

skillChecks.success: The character senses the disrupted earth magic saturating the area. The Ordning's shattering has literally disrupted the flow of elemental earth energy that stone giants tap into for their communion. The Resonance Crystal deep in the cleft is the key — if it can be repaired, the stone giants' sanity will stabilize.
skillChecks.failure: The magical disruption is palpable but its source and nature are unclear.

skillChecks.success: The character sings, plays music, or creates art that resonates with the stone giants' love of creative expression. Kayalithica responds to art when she cannot respond to words, and the creative act pierces through her meditation. 'You make... beautiful things,' she says. 'Perhaps the small ones understand dreaming after all.'
skillChecks.failure: The performance is appreciated but does not break through Kayalithica's dissociative state.

enemies: If the party attacks: 3 Stone Giants (CR 7, HP 126 each, AC 17) — but this is intended to be avoided; the stone giants fight defensively and Kayalithica begs for peace even while under attack
Environmental: a rockslide triggered by the subsonic vibrations — DC 14 Dexterity save or 4d10 bludgeoning damage from falling stones; affects a 20-ft radius area
combatEncounters.difficulty: Deadly (if fought) or None (if handled diplomatically)
combatEncounters.tactics: The stone giants do not want to fight. If attacked, Kayalithica's attendants defend her while she attempts to communicate. They use their rock-throwing ability to create barriers (Wall of Stone effect, 3/day) rather than to harm, and they grapple rather than strike with lethal intent. If the party persists in attacking, Kayalithica retreats into the cleft and seals the entrance with a Stone Shape effect, ending the encounter but losing a potential ally. Attacking the stone giants is a serious mistake that the DM should telegraph clearly.
combatEncounters.terrain: The cleft entrance is a 20-ft wide gap between 300-ft cliff faces. The ground is bare granite, smooth and stable. Kayalithica's meditation shelf is 10 ft above ground level. The cliff faces provide no cover but are climbable (DC 16 Athletics). The subsonic vibrations create difficult terrain within 30 ft of Kayalithica for Small creatures (their inner ear is disrupted). The polished stone walls reflect light and sound unpredictably.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is one of the most important roleplaying scenes in the scenario. Kayalithica is not a quest-giver dispensing exposition — she is a spiritual leader in crisis, struggling to distinguish reality from dreams after her fundamental connection to the world was severed. The party must EARN her attention and trust through creativity, patience, and empathy. Once Kayalithica is grounded in reality, she becomes an invaluable source of information. She explains: (1) The Ordning — the hierarchy of all giantkind — was shattered by Annam All-Father as punishment for the giants' complacency. (2) Every giant race is now scrambling to prove their worth and claim the top of the new hierarchy. (3) The frost giants under Jarl Storvald believe that recovering the Ring of Winter will prove frost giant supremacy. (4) Storvald has captured a cloud giant, Countess Mirran, and is torturing her for information. (5) The stone giants' crisis is spiritual: their communion with the earth was maintained by the Ordning's stability, and without it they are losing their minds. Kayalithica offers a bargain: help her people by repairing the Resonance Crystal in the Dream Galleries, and she will grant passage through the caverns and reveal a hidden water route to Svardborg that bypasses the fortress's surface defenses. If the party includes a character connected to Harshnag, Kayalithica is deeply moved — Harshnag is known among all giant races as one who walks between worlds.
loot: Kayalithica's blessing: a smooth river stone inscribed with a giant rune (functions as a Stone of Good Luck until the next equinox — +1 to ability checks and saving throws while carried)
Stone giant supplies: 8 days of stone giant rations (enormous mushrooms and mineral-rich water — one 'serving' feeds 4 Medium creatures for a day)

Knowledge: complete briefing on the Ordning, frost giant motivations, stone giant crisis, and Storvald's prisoner; this information provides advantage on History and Insight checks related to giant culture for the rest of the scenario

acts.title: Act 2: Deadstone Cleft
acts.description: The second act takes the party deep into the stone giant meditation caverns of Deadstone Cleft. This is a dungeon crawl unlike any other: the 'dungeon' is a living art gallery and spiritual retreat, the 'monsters' are grief-stricken artists driven mad by a metaphysical crisis, and the 'treasure' is knowledge, understanding, and the restoration of a shattered communion between a people and their world. The act balances exploration of the breathtaking Dream Galleries with combat against maddened stone giants and their guardians, and culminates in the puzzle-challenge of repairing the Resonance Crystal. Success here earns the stone giants' aid and reveals the hidden route to Svardborg. The tone should be melancholy and wonder-struck, quite different from the brutal action of Acts 1 and 3.
objectives: Navigate through Deadstone Cleft's meditation chambers
Survive or subdue encounters with maddened stone giants and their guardians
Reach the Dream Galleries and read the prophetic carvings
Repair the Resonance Crystal to restore the stone giants' sanity
Discover the hidden water route to Svardborg

scenes.name: The Shattered Gallery
scenes.description: The party enters Deadstone Cleft and immediately witnesses the devastation the Ordning's shattering has wrought on the stone giant community. The first major chamber is a gallery of historical bas-reliefs — or it was. A maddened stone giant has been systematically destroying the carvings, smashing centuries of artistry into rubble. The giant is not aggressive toward the party; it does not even seem to perceive them. It is locked in a dissociative frenzy, attacking the images on the walls as if they are enemies. The scene is both heartbreaking and dangerous, as the giant's flailing attacks fill the chamber with deadly stone shrapnel. Nearby, two galeb duhr guardians watch the destruction with stony grief but attack anyone who approaches the adjacent meditation chamber where catatonic stone giants sit in helpless silence.
scenes.readAloud: "The passage opens into a cathedral of stone. The chamber is two hundred feet long, sixty feet wide, and its ceiling arches forty feet overhead, supported by natural pillars of granite that have been carved into depictions of ancient stone giant heroes — each one unique, each face rendered with a tenderness that speaks of love as much as skill. The walls are covered in bas-relief carvings that stretch from floor to ceiling: an epic narrative in stone depicting scenes of giant history — the founding of great cities, councils of elders, the working of mountains, the quiet joy of creation. Or they were. A stone giant stands in the center of the gallery, and it is destroying everything. It moves with the jerky, disconnected motions of a marionette — lurching from one wall panel to the next, raising its enormous fists, and bringing them down on the carvings with devastating force. Each blow sends cracks racing across centuries of artwork. Chunks of carved stone the size of your head fly through the air with lethal velocity. And the giant is weeping. Thick mineral tears streak its granite face as it destroys its heritage with its own hands, and its mouth moves in a constant, keening moan that reverberates through the chamber like the grief of the mountain itself. 'Wrong,' it groans between blows. 'All wrong. The pattern is broken. The stone lies. THE STONE LIES.' It brings both fists down on a panel depicting a stone giant elder in meditation, and the entire section of wall collapses inward, revealing a dark passage beyond. The giant does not notice. It has already moved to the next panel. In the adjacent chamber, visible through an archway, you can see two squat, boulder-like shapes — galeb duhr — positioned before a group of motionless stone giants who sit in perfect stillness, their eyes closed, their faces slack. The galeb duhr turn to face your approach with expressions that, on a face made of living rock, somehow convey both sorrow and warning."

skillChecks.success: Using knowledge of stone giant culture (gained from Kayalithica or a DC 16 History check), the character speaks to the giant in terms it can understand — addressing its grief, acknowledging the beauty of what was created, affirming that the stone does not lie even when the pattern changes. The giant stops, trembling, and sinks to its knees. It does not speak again but it stops destroying, and it does not impede the party's passage.
skillChecks.failure: The giant does not respond to words. It continues its destructive frenzy, ignoring the party unless they physically intervene.

skillChecks.success: The character navigates through the gallery without being struck by flying debris.
skillChecks.failure: A chunk of carved stone strikes the character: 2d8 bludgeoning damage.

skillChecks.success: Despite the destruction, the character reads enough of the surviving carvings to understand the narrative: the stone giants' entire cultural identity is built around their communion with the earth, and the Ordning's shattering has broken that communion. The carvings also hint at a solution — a 'heartstone' deep in the mountain that maintains the connection.
skillChecks.failure: The destruction is too extensive. The surviving fragments are beautiful but their narrative context is lost.

skillChecks.skill: Animal Handling or Nature (approaching the galeb duhr)
skillChecks.success: The character approaches the galeb duhr guardians with appropriate deference, moving slowly and making no threatening gestures. The galeb duhr recognize the character's respect and allow passage to the meditation chamber, though they watch closely for any sign of threat to their charges.
skillChecks.failure: The galeb duhr interpret the approach as a threat and attack, rolling forward with grinding force.

enemies: 1 Maddened Stone Giant (CR 7, HP 126, AC 17) — fights only if physically restrained or attacked; otherwise continues destroying carvings and is a source of environmental hazard (stone shrapnel: 2d8 bludgeoning in 15-ft radius around it each round, DC 14 Dex save for half)

2 Galeb Duhr (CR 6, HP 85 each, AC 16) — fight to protect the catatonic stone giants; they use their animate boulders ability to create additional combatants (2 animated boulders, effectively additional galeb duhr with HP 40 each)
combatEncounters.tactics: The maddened stone giant is not directing its attacks at the party and does not use tactical thinking. It is an environmental hazard that also happens to hit very hard if the party tries to physically restrain it (Multiattack: 2 fist attacks, +9 to hit, 3d8+6 bludgeoning). The galeb duhr are the real tactical combat: they fight defensively, using animated boulders as front-line combatants while they protect the meditation chamber entrance. They use their rolling charge attack (bonus action, 2d10+4 bludgeoning and DC 14 Str save or prone) against anyone who gets close. They can also cast Stone Shape to block passages or create barriers. If one galeb duhr is destroyed, the other fights more desperately but can be convinced to stand down with a DC 16 Persuasion check and a demonstration that the party means no harm to the sleeping giants.
combatEncounters.terrain: The gallery is 200 ft long, 60 ft wide, with a 40-ft ceiling. Carved pillars (half cover, AC 17, HP 80) are spaced every 30 ft. The floor is covered in rubble from the destroyed carvings (difficult terrain throughout). The archway to the meditation chamber is 15 ft wide and can be blocked by galeb duhr Stone Shape. The hidden passage revealed by the collapse is 10 ft wide and descends at a 30-degree angle into darkness — this leads deeper toward the Dream Galleries. Flying debris from the maddened giant affects a 15-ft radius around it and moves each round as the giant moves along the walls.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This scene should be deeply affecting. The maddened stone giant is not a villain — it is a grief-stricken artist destroying its own people's history because its connection to truth (the earth, the stone) has been severed. The galeb duhr are not enemies — they are loyal guardians desperately protecting their vulnerable charges. Every combat in this scene is avoidable with the right approach, and the DM should reward creative, empathetic solutions. If the party calms the maddened giant and earns the galeb duhr's trust, both events provide tangible benefits: the calmed giant gestures toward the descending passage (showing the way to the Dream Galleries), and the galeb duhr offer a gift — a polished stone that functions as a one-use casting of Pass Without Trace. The catatonic stone giants in the meditation chamber cannot be awakened by normal means; only repairing the Resonance Crystal will bring them back. A Detect Magic spell or DC 14 Arcana check reveals that their spirits are not absent — they are lost in the dream-space between the material world and the elemental earth, unable to find their way back.
loot: Fragments of the destroyed carvings: 6 pieces of exquisitely carved stone worth 15 gp each to a collector, or priceless to the stone giants (returning these later earns additional gratitude)
Galeb duhr gift (if earned through diplomacy): a Polished River Stone that casts Pass Without Trace once before crumbling to dust

From the hidden passage (revealed by the wall collapse): a niche containing a Stone Giant artisan's toolkit — masterwork mason's tools worth 100 gp, and a chisel made of adamantine that functions as a +1 dagger (1d4+1 piercing, can carve any non-magical material)

scenes.name: The Heart of the Mountain
scenes.description: The party descends through the hidden passage into the Dream Galleries — the deepest and most sacred chambers of Deadstone Cleft. Here, the living bas-reliefs tell the complete story of giantkind, and the Resonance Crystal awaits repair. This scene combines puzzle-solving (reading the carvings for clues, understanding the crystal's function), environmental challenges (the dream fog, phantom visions), and a potential combat with the Dream Guardian. Repairing the crystal is the central objective of Act 2, and success here transforms the stone giants from a tragic obstacle into a powerful ally. The Dream Galleries should feel like entering another world — a place where time moves differently, reality is negotiable, and the boundary between past and present dissolves.
scenes.readAloud: "The passage descends for what feels like hours, the stone growing warmer and the air thicker with each step. Crystal veins in the walls begin to glow — softly at first, then with increasing intensity, casting shifting patterns of blue, amber, and violet light that move across the stone like living things. The subsonic hum you felt at the surface is stronger here, a vibration that syncs with your heartbeat until you cannot tell where your pulse ends and the mountain's begins. And then the passage opens, and your breath catches. The Dream Galleries stretch before you like a cathedral built by gods. The ceiling is lost in shadow a hundred feet above. The walls — every surface, every pillar, every arch — are covered in carvings of such extraordinary detail and beauty that your mind struggles to process them. But these carvings are not static. In your peripheral vision, they MOVE. A scene depicting a stone giant shaping a mountain shifts and flows like a slow river — you can see the giant's hands moving, see the mountain rising, see the stone bending to the artist's will. When you look directly, the carvings are still. When you look away, they live. The air smells of mineral and lightning — the scent of deep earth magic. And at the far end of the galleries, pulsing with a rhythm that matches the mountain's heartbeat, is the Resonance Crystal. It fills a natural alcove like a frozen explosion of light — a formation of interlocking crystal shafts ten feet tall, each one humming at a different frequency, creating a chord of subsonic vibration that you feel in your marrow. But the chord is wrong. Dissonant. One of the central crystal shafts is cracked from base to tip, a jagged fracture that bleeds light like a wound. The break is fresh — weeks, maybe — and the wrongness of it resonates through the galleries like a scream in a library. This is it. This is what broke the stone giants. And this is what you must fix."

skillChecks.success: The character resists the hypnotic effect of the living carvings and maintains full awareness.
skillChecks.failure: The character is charmed for 1 hour, wandering among the carvings in a dreamlike trance. They are not hostile but are unresponsive and vulnerable. Taking damage ends the effect.

skillChecks.success: The character reads and interprets the prophetic carvings on the deepest wall. They depict possible futures: in one, all giant races war against each other until only ruins remain. In another, a small group of diverse creatures — including figures the size of humans — stands before a storm giant king, and the Ordning is restored. The carving suggests the key is gathering proof from each giant stronghold (the conch shells) and presenting them at Maelstrom.
skillChecks.failure: The carvings are beautiful but opaque. The character cannot interpret the prophetic symbolism.

skillChecks.success: The character understands the crystal's function: it is a focus for elemental earth energy, maintaining the stone giants' spiritual connection to the world. The crack disrupts the harmonic frequencies. Repair requires either powerful earth magic (Stone Shape cast at 5th level or higher, or Mending combined with a DC 15 Arcana check to channel earth energy) or physical repair using adamantine tools and a DC 18 mason's tools check. The adamantine chisel from the Shattered Gallery works perfectly for this purpose.
skillChecks.failure: The crystal is clearly important and clearly broken, but the character cannot determine how to repair it.

skillChecks.skill: Mason's Tools (repairing the crystal, requires adamantine chisel or equivalent)
skillChecks.success: The character carefully works the crack closed, using the adamantine chisel to score guide-lines and then applying pressure at precisely calculated points. The crystal's hum shifts from dissonance to harmony. A wave of warmth pulses through the mountain. Somewhere above, in the galleries they left behind, stone giants gasp awake from their catatonia. The maddened giant stops its destruction and weeps with relief. The mountain sighs.
skillChecks.failure: The repair attempt worsens the crack by a fraction. The character can try again with disadvantage, or another approach must be found. A second failure shatters the crystal permanently (this should be telegraphed clearly to give the party a chance to stop).

skillChecks.success: Channeling magic into the crystal while casting Mending (or Stone Shape, or any earth-related spell) seals the crack. The effect is the same as the mason's tools repair.
skillChecks.failure: The magic dissipates against the crystal without effect. The character senses they need a more focused approach — perhaps combining magic with physical repair.

enemies: Dream Guardian — Galeb Duhr Elder (AC 18, HP 120, Speed 30 ft, STR 22, DEX 8, CON 20, INT 14, WIS 18, CHA 12; Attacks: Slam +9, 3d8+6 bludgeoning; Stone Shape 3/day, Wall of Stone 1/day; Animate Boulders 1/day summons 3 animated boulders; Resistance to nonmagical bludgeoning/slashing/piercing; Immune to poison; Tremorsense 120 ft)
2 Animated Boulders (AC 17, HP 60 each, Slam +6, 2d8+4 bludgeoning) — summoned by Dream Guardian if combat begins

Phantom Visions — illusory warriors from the prophetic carvings; Phantasmal Force effect on all creatures in 20-ft radius when certain carvings are disturbed; DC 15 Intelligence save or perceive phantom warriors as real for 1 minute, taking 1d6 psychic damage per round
combatEncounters.tactics: The Dream Guardian challenges anyone approaching the Resonance Crystal. It is not mindlessly hostile — it speaks in slow, rumbling Giant: 'The heartstone must not be touched by those who do not dream in stone.' It can be bypassed by demonstrating knowledge of stone giant customs (DC 14 Religion), showing the calmed maddened giant followed the party (proof of good intent), presenting Kayalithica's blessing stone, or simply explaining the intent to repair the crystal (DC 16 Persuasion). If combat begins, the Dream Guardian fights defensively, using Wall of Stone to protect the crystal and Animate Boulders to engage the party at range. It uses Stone Shape to reshape the terrain — collapsing paths, raising barriers, creating difficult terrain. If reduced to half HP, it pauses and asks: 'You fight hard. But do you fight to destroy, or to heal? Show me your intent.' A DC 14 Persuasion check at this point ends the combat immediately.
combatEncounters.terrain: The Dream Galleries are 100 ft wide and extend 300 ft from the entrance to the crystal alcove. Crystal veins in the walls provide dim light throughout. The floor is smooth stone, not difficult terrain. Carved pillars (half cover) are spaced every 20 ft. The crystal alcove is a natural recess 30 ft across, partially blocked by crystal formations that provide three-quarters cover. The living bas-reliefs on the walls can be disturbed by loud noises or stray attacks, potentially triggering Phantom Vision events. The dream fog fills the space but has no mechanical effect beyond the initial save upon entry.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is the emotional climax of Act 2 and one of the most important scenes in the scenario. The Dream Galleries should feel sacred — a place of immense beauty and deep sorrow. The living carvings tell a story of creation, pride, communion, and loss that parallels the current crisis. The DM should describe specific carvings in detail: a stone giant shaping a mountain with bare hands, a council of giant races in harmony, the moment the Ordning was established (all giants kneeling before a towering figure of lightning — Annam All-Father). The prophetic carvings are key plot hooks: they foreshadow the campaign's direction and give the party a sense of purpose beyond 'kill the bad giants.' The Resonance Crystal repair is the scenario's most satisfying moment if done well — describe the harmonic shift, the warmth flowing through the mountain, the sense of a wound healing. When the crystal is repaired, Kayalithica's voice echoes through the cleft: 'The dream lives again. Small ones, you have done what we could not. The stone remembers, and we remember with it. Come. We will show you the way beneath the ice.' This is the transition to Act 3: the stone giants reveal the underground river passage to Svardborg. They also gift the party the Dream Crystal — a fragment of the Resonance Crystal that grants one use of Contact Other Plane.
loot: Dream Crystal (one use of Contact Other Plane without risk of madness — the crystal channels the question through the earth itself, receiving answers from the accumulated wisdom of stone giant generations)
Galeb duhr elder's gratitude (if combat ended peacefully or never began): a fist-sized geode that functions as a Gem of Brightness with 20 charges
Prophetic knowledge: detailed understanding of the campaign's larger arc, granting advantage on Intelligence checks related to the Ordning and giant politics for the remainder of the campaign
Stone giant artisan's legacy (found in a niche near the crystal): a set of Goggles of Night wrapped in stone-fiber cloth, left by an artisan who worked in the deepest, darkest galleries
Crystal fragments: 6 small resonance crystal shards worth 50 gp each, or priceless as spell components for earth-related magic (DM discretion — advantage on one spell with earth themes)

acts.title: Act 3: Svardborg
acts.description: The final act takes the party from the relative safety of the stone giant caverns into the frozen heart of Jarl Storvald's iceberg-fortress. The underground river passage discovered by the stone giants provides a hidden entrance to Svardborg's submerged levels, bypassing the surface defenses and depositing the party directly below the prison cells where Countess Mirran is held. The act is a military infiltration: the party must navigate the ice tunnels, free Mirran, locate the Conch of Teleportation in Storvald's war room, and either escape or confront the Jarl directly. The frost giant fortress is a much more dangerous environment than any the party has faced — the inhabitants are CR 8 elite warriors, the environment itself is hostile (extreme cold, slippery ice, freezing water), and Jarl Storvald is a formidable opponent driven by obsession. Multiple approaches are viable: stealth, diplomacy (challenging Storvald to a contest of strength), sabotage (threatening the iceberg's structural integrity), or direct assault (extremely dangerous but possible, especially with Mirran as an ally).
objectives: Enter Svardborg through the underground river passage
Navigate the ice tunnels to the prison level
Free Countess Mirran from her cell
Recover the Conch of Teleportation from Storvald's war room
Confront, outmaneuver, or escape Jarl Storvald
Escape Svardborg with allies and artifacts intact

scenes.name: The River Beneath the Ice
scenes.description: The stone giants' hidden river passage carries the party through miles of subterranean waterway, emerging through a natural fissure in the iceberg's submerged section. The journey is dangerous — the water is icy cold, the passage is partially submerged, and the transition from stone to ice is disorienting. The party arrives in the lowest level of Svardborg, a rarely-visited maintenance area where meltwater is collected and the iceberg's natural cold-water spring maintains the fortress's structural integrity. This scene is about the journey itself and the initial exploration of the fortress's weakest point.
scenes.readAloud: "The underground river carries you north through absolute darkness. Kayalithica's stone giant guide — a young giant named Haldorr who volunteered for the journey — poles the crude stone raft with steady, methodical strokes, his grey form barely visible in the crystal-glow of the resonance shard he carries. The water is shockingly cold even through the raft's stone hull, and the air temperature drops steadily as you travel. After what feels like hours, Haldorr stops. 'The stone ends here,' he rumbles, touching the tunnel ceiling. 'Beyond this point, the mountain becomes ice. The river flows into the frozen place — the fortress of the frost-walkers. I cannot follow. Stone giants do not belong in ice.' He places his massive hand against the tunnel wall one final time, and the rock glows faintly under his touch. 'The small ones were brave in the dreaming place. Be brave now in the frozen place. And return, if you can. We would hear the story.' He pushes the raft forward into the narrowing passage and the stone gives way to ice — a sudden, shocking transition from the warm mineral solidity of the earth to the sterile, crystalline hardness of ancient ice. The resonance shard's glow refracts through the frozen walls in patterns of blue and white, and the silence is absolute except for the soft lapping of the river against the ice. The passage narrows, dips, and for a terrifying thirty feet is completely submerged — you must hold your breath and pull yourselves along the ice ceiling to reach the air pocket on the other side. Then the passage opens into a low, wide chamber of ice. Icicles hang from the ceiling like the teeth of some enormous beast. The air is so cold that every breath creates a cloud of crystals. And you can hear, echoing through the ice from somewhere above, the voices of frost giants."

skillChecks.success: The character endures the submerged section without difficulty, emerging cold but functional.
skillChecks.failure: The shock of the frigid water overwhelms the character: 3d6 cold damage and the character gains 1 level of exhaustion.

skillChecks.success: The character navigates the submerged passage efficiently, taking only 1 round.
skillChecks.failure: The character struggles against the current and the cold, taking 2 rounds to cross. If they fail the Constitution save as well, they risk drowning (begin suffocating after rounds equal to CON modifier, minimum 1).

skillChecks.success: The character spots the cold-water spring — a natural upwelling of frigid seawater that keeps the iceberg from melting from within. They also notice that the maintenance level is largely unpatrolled, with only old ice mephit tracks suggesting occasional visitors.
skillChecks.failure: The chamber appears empty and unremarkable. The spring is not noticed.

skillChecks.success: Using the echoes of giant voices and the draft of air from above, the character plots a route upward through the ice tunnels toward the prison level.
skillChecks.failure: The disorienting reflective ice makes navigation difficult. The party takes a wrong turn and encounters an additional patrol (2 ice mephits) before finding the correct route.

enemies: 4 Ice Mephits (CR 1/2, HP 21 each, AC 11) — encountered in the maintenance level if the party makes noise; they are servants, not warriors, and attempt to flee to raise the alarm rather than fight
If alarm raised: 1 Frost Giant (CR 8, HP 138, AC 15) descends to investigate within 5 minutes
combatEncounters.difficulty: Easy (mephits) to Deadly (if the frost giant arrives)
combatEncounters.tactics: The ice mephits scatter in four directions, each trying to reach a different exit. They use Frost Breath (DC 10 Dex, 2d4 cold) as a parting shot and then flee at full speed. They can squeeze through gaps too narrow for Medium creatures. If even one escapes, the fortress goes on alert within 10 minutes. The frost giant investigator is cautious — it enters the maintenance level with a torch and searches methodically, and can be ambushed from behind ice formations with a DC 14 Stealth check. However, a frost giant fight in the cramped maintenance level is extremely dangerous due to the confined space and the proximity of the cold-water spring (any explosion or large-scale destruction risks the spring).
combatEncounters.terrain: The maintenance level is a 40 ft x 60 ft natural ice chamber with a 10-ft ceiling — too low for frost giants to stand fully upright, which gives them disadvantage on melee attacks. The cold-water spring occupies a 10-ft pool in the center (contact with the water: 4d6 cold damage per round). Ice formations around the chamber provide half cover. The floor is solid ice (DC 12 Acrobatics for full movement in combat). Four narrow passages lead upward to different sections of the fortress.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This scene marks the transition from the wonder of the stone giant caverns to the deadly tension of the frost giant fortress. The farewell with Haldorr should be brief but meaningful — his admiration for the party's courage is genuine, and his parting gift of the resonance shard (provides dim light in a 10-ft radius and prevents exhaustion from cold for 8 hours, then goes dark) is practical. The submerged passage is the most dangerous environmental challenge so far and should be played for genuine tension — describe the crushing cold, the darkness, the ice pressing in from all sides. Once inside Svardborg, the tone shifts to military thriller: the party is behind enemy lines, outnumbered and outpowered, and every noise could bring a frost giant crashing down on them. The DM should track the alarm status meticulously — a fortress on alert is exponentially harder to navigate than one that is not.
loot: Haldorr's gift: a Resonance Shard (provides dim light 10 ft, prevents cold exhaustion for 8 hours, then becomes inert — but remains a beautiful crystal worth 25 gp)

Maintenance level supplies: frost giant tools for ice-shaping (functionally identical to mason's tools but for ice; worth 50 gp), a frozen barrel containing preserved whale meat (5 days of rations for 6 Medium creatures)
From ice mephits (if defeated): each carries a tiny ice gem worth 5 gp that melts in 24 hours unless kept below freezing

scenes.name: The Prisoner and the Jarl
scenes.description: The climactic scene of the scenario brings together multiple threads: the party must free Countess Mirran, confront or outmaneuver Jarl Storvald, and secure the Conch of Teleportation. This scene is designed to be resolved in multiple ways, and the party's approach through the earlier acts determines which options are available. A stealthy party can free Mirran and steal the conch without ever facing Storvald directly. A diplomatic party can challenge Storvald to a contest of strength (a frost giant tradition) and win the conch through cultural engagement. A combat-oriented party can fight through the Great Hall with Mirran as an ally. And a clever party can threaten the iceberg's structural integrity as leverage. The scene should feel like the culmination of everything the party has learned and earned throughout the scenario.
scenes.readAloud: "The prison cells are carved into the ice below the Great Hall, accessible by a spiraling ramp of frozen steps wide enough for a giant to descend. Two frost giant guards stand at the base, their greataxes crossed before a barred door of iron so cold it smokes in the ambient air. Beyond the bars, you see her — Countess Mirran of the cloud giants. She is twenty-two feet tall, and even sitting slumped against the ice wall of her cell, she dwarfs the frost giants who hold her. But she is diminished. Her cloud-grey skin is mottled with bruises. Her silver hair, which must once have flowed like morning mist, is matted and tangled. Chains of black iron — enchanted against teleportation, from the runes that crawl along their surface — bind her wrists and ankles to the wall. Her robes, once fine silk the color of sunset, are torn and stained. And her eyes — when she lifts her head and sees you through the bars — her eyes hold a desperate, burning intelligence that even weeks of captivity and torture have not extinguished. She does not speak. She looks at you, then looks at the guards, then looks at you again. And very, very slightly, she nods. She is ready. She has been waiting for exactly this moment. Above you, through the ice ceiling, you hear the rumble of giant voices, the clash of drinking horns, the howl of winter wolves. The feast is in full swing. Jarl Storvald sits on his frozen throne, surrounded by warriors, obsessing over an artifact he will never find. And here, in the ice prison below his feet, the key to his undoing waits in chains."

skillChecks.success: The party reaches striking distance of the guards without being detected, gaining a surprise round.
skillChecks.failure: The guards hear the party's approach on the ice floor and ready their weapons. No surprise.

skillChecks.success: The lock opens cleanly. Mirran rises to her full height — twenty-two feet of cloud giant fury barely contained — and whispers in accented Common: 'The chains too. The chains bind my magic.'
skillChecks.failure: The lock resists. The character can try again, but the noise requires a DC 14 Stealth check to avoid alerting additional patrols.

skillChecks.success: The character identifies the chains' enchantment and disrupts it with a careful application of Dispel Magic (automatic) or a counter-rune scratched into the ice (DC 17 Arcana). The chains fall away. Mirran gasps as her magic returns — the air around her swirls with miniature clouds, and her bruises begin to fade as natural cloud giant regeneration kicks in.
skillChecks.failure: The enchantment resists mundane efforts. The chains can only be removed by destroying the locks (AC 19, HP 25 each, immune to cold damage) or by Dispel Magic cast at 4th level or higher.

skillChecks.success: The character invokes frost giant tradition (learned from Kayalithica or from captured frost giants) and challenges Storvald to a contest of strength. If the Jarl accepts (and he will, because refusing would shame him before his warriors), the party can compete in a series of three tests: arm wrestling (Athletics), endurance (Constitution), and a duel to first blood (combat, but nonlethal). Winning 2 of 3 earns the party the right to claim one item from Storvald's hoard — including the conch.
skillChecks.failure: Storvald laughs contemptuously. 'Small ones do not challenge Jarls. Small ones are food for wolves.' Combat begins.
