skillChecks.success: The character reveals knowledge of the cold-water spring and threatens to destroy it, which would crack the iceberg and sink Svardborg within an hour. Storvald, whose entire power base is literally this fortress, goes pale with fury — but also with fear. He demands proof. If the party can demonstrate they have access to the spring (via the maintenance level), Storvald agrees to negotiate rather than risk losing everything.
skillChecks.failure: Storvald does not believe the threat. 'You lie. No small creature could harm Svardborg.' Combat begins.

enemies: Prison guards: 2 Frost Giants (CR 8, HP 138 each, AC 15)

If alarm is raised or combat reaches the Great Hall: Jarl Storvald (use Frost Giant stats with HP 180, AC 16 — enchanted chain shirt, +10 to hit with greataxe for 3d12+7 slashing, Icy Command 1/day — all frost giants within 60 ft gain advantage on their next attack) + 2 Frost Giant Warriors (CR 8, HP 138 each) + 4 Winter Wolves (CR 3, HP 75 each)

Countess Mirran as ally (if freed): Cloud Giant (CR 9, HP 200, AC 14, Morningstar +12 for 3d8+8 bludgeoning, Rock +12 range 60/240 for 4d10+8; can cast Fog Cloud 3/day, Misty Step 3/day, Feather Fall at will)
combatEncounters.difficulty: Deadly (without Mirran) / Hard (with Mirran as ally)
combatEncounters.tactics: The prison guards fight to prevent the party from reaching Mirran's cell — they position themselves to block the cell door and use their greataxes in the narrow corridor (advantage on attacks due to chokepoint). If the alarm is raised, Storvald arrives in 3 rounds with his retinue. Storvald is a tactician: he orders winter wolves to flank, warriors to form a shield wall, and reserves his Icy Command for when the party is most committed to melee. He fights with furious intensity but is also paranoid — if Mirran is freed, he splits his attention between the party and her, reducing his tactical effectiveness. Mirran, once freed, fights with terrifying competence. She uses Fog Cloud to obscure the party's position, Misty Step to reposition, and her morningstar to devastating effect. She focuses on Storvald personally — she has weeks of rage to express. If Storvald is reduced to 60 HP or below, he attempts to flee to his war room to retrieve the conch and teleport to Maelstrom for reinforcements. If he reaches the war room, he grabs the conch in 1 round and activates it in 2 — the party has 3 rounds to stop him. If Storvald is defeated, his remaining warriors retreat to the longship harbor and flee on the fastest ship.
combatEncounters.terrain: The prison level is a narrow ice corridor (10 ft wide, 15 ft tall) with 4 cells on each side. The spiral ramp to the Great Hall is 15 ft wide and ascends 30 ft. The Great Hall is 100 ft long, 60 ft wide, with 40-ft ice ceilings. Ice pillars (half cover) are every 20 ft. Storvald's ice throne radiates cold (1d6 cold per round within 10 ft). The floor is ice (DC 12 Acrobatics for full movement in combat). The war room is behind the Great Hall through a 15-ft corridor guarded by the 2 frost giant guards described in the Storvald's War Room location entry. The hall contains a massive whalebone feast table (full cover if overturned, DC 18 Athletics to flip) and scattered furniture that can serve as improvised cover.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This scene is the scenario's climax and should feel appropriately momentous. Countess Mirran is the emotional anchor: her rescue is a genuine act of heroism, and her gratitude is profound and lasting. She speaks with the formal, slightly archaic diction of cloud giant nobility: 'You have broken my chains and restored my honor. My debt to you is written in the ice of this place and will not melt until it is repaid.' If the party negotiates rather than fights, Mirran still needs to be freed first (Storvald will not release her willingly under any circumstances — she is his only lead to the Ring of Winter). Jarl Storvald is a complex antagonist. He is not mindlessly evil — he is a proud warrior-king driven to extremes by desperation. The Ordning's shattering threatened everything he built, and the Ring of Winter represents his only plan to restore frost giant supremacy. His treatment of Mirran is cruel, but in his mind it is justified by the stakes. If the party defeats him, his last words should reflect this complexity: 'The ice will remember... even if you do not. The Ordning must... be restored. At any cost.' The Conch of Teleportation discovery is the second major plot advancement of the campaign, confirming the path to Maelstrom. Mirran explains that the storm giant court is in crisis — King Hekaton has disappeared, and his daughter Serissa is trying to hold power against scheming siblings. The conchs are keys to the court, and presenting them shows the party has confronted the giant crisis firsthand. After the encounter, the party can escape Svardborg through the maintenance level, by longship, or via the conch itself (though Mirran advises saving it for the right moment). Svardborg does not collapse with Storvald's defeat — the fortress endures, but the frost giant raids cease as the surviving warriors have no leader to drive them.

Frost Brand Longsword (rare, requires attunement — found in Storvald's shrine to Thrym; +1d6 cold damage, resistance to fire damage, sheds bright light 10 ft and dim light 10 ft more when temperature is 32 F or below)
Cloak of the Manta Ray (uncommon — hidden in Storvald's quarters; grants swim speed 60 ft and underwater breathing while worn with hood up)

Storvald's treasure hoard: 600 gp, 1,800 sp, a platinum-and-sapphire ring worth 500 gp, a block of never-melting ice worth 500 gp, a set of whale-ivory chess pieces worth 250 gp, and navigation charts showing all frost giant operations on the Sea of Moving Ice

Mirran's gratitude: the cloud giant countess pledges a favor to be called in at the party's need — she can provide aerial transportation via cloud castle, intelligence about cloud giant politics, or direct combat assistance in one future encounter

From frost giant warriors (if fought): 3-6 greataxes (giant-sized, 50 gp each as scrap), chain shirts (giant-sized, 75 gp each as raw materials), 3d10 gp per giant, drinking horns of carved bone worth 15 gp each

Storvald's personal journal (written in Giant): complete intelligence about frost giant operations, the search for the Ring of Winter, and correspondence with the Arcane Brotherhood — worth 200 gp to the Harpers, Lords' Alliance, or any intelligence-gathering faction

rewards.xp: Total XP breakdown per party member (assuming 4-member party): Act 1 Iron Inlet combat ~700 XP each; Act 1 stone giant encounter (if fought, not recommended) ~600 XP each; Act 2 Shattered Gallery encounters ~500 XP each; Act 2 Dream Gallery (Dream Guardian + phantoms) ~400 XP each; Act 2 milestone for repairing Resonance Crystal: 600 XP each; Act 3 Entry and navigation ~300 XP each; Act 3 Prison guards ~350 XP each; Act 3 Storvald encounter ~900 XP each; Act 3 milestone for freeing Mirran: 500 XP each; Scenario completion milestone: 750 XP each. Total combat + milestone: approximately 4,000-5,000 XP per party member, sufficient to advance from level 7 to level 9 over the course of the scenario.

storyRewards: Stone giant alliance — Thane Kayalithica and the restored Deadstone Cleft community are grateful allies who provide sanctuary, intelligence about giant movements, and potential military support in future scenarios

Countess Mirran's pledge — a cloud giant noblewoman owes the party a significant favor, callable at any time; she provides access to cloud giant society, aerial transportation, and formidable combat power
Frost giant intelligence — Storvald's journal and war room documents provide comprehensive knowledge of frost giant operations, the Ring of Winter search, and Arcane Brotherhood involvement

Knowledge of the Ordning — through Kayalithica's teaching and the prophetic carvings, the party now understands the fundamental crisis of giantkind and has seen a vision of its resolution at Maelstrom

dmTips: The tonal shift between the three acts is the key to this scenario's impact. Act 1 is visceral and immediate — frost giant raids, burning villages, military threat. Act 2 is contemplative and wondrous — sacred caverns, living art, spiritual crisis. Act 3 is tense and strategic — infiltration, prisoner rescue, confrontation with power. Each act should feel distinct, and the transitions between them should be deliberate. Do not rush from one act to the next; let the players absorb the atmosphere of each setting.

The stone giant sections are the heart of the scenario and the most challenging to run well. Stone giants are not dumb brutes — they are contemplative artists and spiritual practitioners who happen to be twenty feet tall. Kayalithica should feel like a wise elder in crisis, not a quest-dispensing NPC. The maddened giants should evoke sympathy, not just combat instincts. If the players choose to fight through Deadstone Cleft rather than engage with the stone giants' story, they miss the scenario's best content and lose access to the hidden route to Svardborg. Reward empathy and punish murder-hobo tendencies.

Frost giants are the most militarily competent giant race the party has faced. Unlike hill giants (stupid), ogres (brutal), or stone giants (pacifistic), frost giants are disciplined warriors with coordinated tactics, military hierarchy, and strategic thinking. They should feel like fighting a professional army, not a rabble. Describe their formation fighting, their signal horns, their coordinated wolf-and-giant tactics. The party should feel genuinely outmatched in a straight fight and incentivized to use stealth, diplomacy, or the environment.

Countess Mirran is a CR 9 ally who can shift the final battle dramatically. If freed, she is motivated and powerful — but also injured and emotionally volatile. The DM should play her as competent but not invincible: she makes tactical decisions, but her hatred of Storvald sometimes overrides sound judgment. She is not a party member the players control; she is an NPC ally the DM runs. Let her do impressive things, but do not let her solve the encounter single-handedly.

Cold weather mechanics matter in this scenario. Do not hand-wave the environment. Track rations, check for cold exposure, describe the physical misery of operating in sub-zero temperatures. The Resonance Shard from Haldorr protects against exhaustion for 8 hours — make sure the party knows this has a time limit and plans accordingly. Cold resistance (from spells, items, or winter wolf pelts) should feel genuinely valuable.
